page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance operating on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, it delivers 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs with dedicated CPU allocation. Cache layout includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Advanced instruction set support includes AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and standard AVX vector extensions.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.c7a.4xlarge within average performance tiers for general compute tasks. Synthetic testing with stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark places single-core and multi-core processor performance consistently in the middle distribution range. The instance achieved 15.82 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 14.05 GB/sec in static web serving, and a Geekbench software compilation score of 13374.0. In machine learning workloads, prompt processing for small and medium LLM models yielded standard results, while small-model text generation performed strongly at 301.48 tokens per second. Performance trade-offs manifest primarily in memory bandwidth under heavy uncached access, where large-block read operations achieved 23.77 GB/sec and write operations recorded 12.96 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU specification delivers a cost-efficient hardware profile for processing-intensive tasks that do not require high memory density per core. Because local storage is absent, instances can be attached to external network storage options scaled separately from compute resources. This instance type is well suited for CI/CD software compilation, web server hosting, microservice backends, batch processing, and lightweight inference services.

Performance benchmarks show consistent middle-tier scores across single-core and multi-core operations, including software compilation, web serving, and Redis database tests. The dedicated CPU allocation offers efficient execution for processor-heavy applications. Recommended workloads include software build pipelines, web serving, microservices, and general compute processing.
